result.title: Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as synthetic participants in opinion-dynamics experiments, often assuming that an agent's behaviour is fully determined by its prompt. We test this assumption with a framework in which LLM agents discuss a contested policy issue over repeated rounds while their stance is quantified by a fixed psychometric instrument independent of any dynamics model. Across six LLMs, committed personas are intrinsically stable: in each of the five models tested without peer input, every agent keeps its assigned side for 20 rounds. The observed loss of alignment under discussion is therefore interaction-induced, we call it alignment drift, and model-specific: gpt-4.1 keeps opinion clusters apart, claude-sonnet-5 holds them partially, and gpt-5.6-sol and claude-opus-5 abandon them. Under selective attention, one LLM maintains separated opinion clusters under stance-homophilous attention. Qualitative profiles persist at doubled population and horizon and on a second issue. Such heterogeneity makes the LLM choice a first-class validity variable for social simulation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建一个让 LLM 代理就争议政策进行多轮讨论的框架，用独立于动力学模型的固定心理测量工具量化立场，考察六个模型在同伴输入下出现的「alignment drift」，发现该漂移是交互诱发且模型特异的。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用独立固定探针追踪多轮交互中内部立场漂移、并报告模型特异差异的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 多轮 latent 更新或循环计算中的状态漂移与探针稳定性评估，但与视觉推理无直接联系。
